item.title: Tinubu returns 1m out-of-school children to classrooms – APC PCC
item.description: …Says NELFUND disbursed ₦372.62bn in student loans By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu’s administration has returned over one million out-of-school children to classrooms. The Council said this in a statement on Wednesday by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, citing the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) 2026 report of the Federal Ministry of Education. The report credits the Better Education Service Delivery for All (BESDA) programme for the feat. It also says the programme trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and set up 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states. The Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) has reached 7.19 million girls, of whom 3.7 million are enrolled in secondary schools. Over 10,000 schools have also benefited from improved facilities, according to the council. On funding, the Federal Government reportedly allocated a record ₦3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget. It also secured $552 million for a basic education programme targeting 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools. According to the council, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund NELFUND has processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed ₦372.62 billion. Of this, ₦192.89 billion went to tuition and ₦179.73 billion to upkeep allowances, across 319 tertiary institutions. The statement said the administration has resolved the age-long dispute with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and implemented the agreement providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits. The Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund, it added, has paid out ₦28 billion to 15,000 workers in 153 public institutions. Eligible staff can access loans of up to ₦10 million for housing, healthcare, transportation and education. On technical and vocational education and training (TVET), the scheme has drawn over 2.8 million applications. A total of 156,446 verified trainees are receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support. Alake said more than ₦65.7 billion has been disbursed to trainees and ₦30.2 billion to training centres. Thirty-eight technical colleges have been rehabilitated, and technical education now covers tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms at no cost to students. On teacher development, Alake said 53,553 teachers have registered under EduRevamp, and 51,794 have joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP). The six-month programme offers professional qualifications, certification and licensing. Backed by ₦2 billion, it targets 250,000 teachers by 2027, he added. Alake added that in medical education, ₦110 billion is going into rehabilitating 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones. item.title: ‘We have kissed empty Mondays goodbye’ — Mbah on IPOB sit-at-home in Enugu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah says residents have overcome the fear that kept roads and communities quiet on Mondays during the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) sit-at-home campaign, pointing to security measures along key routes in the state. Mbah spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign flag-off in Nsukka on Wednesday, saying the change meant people could travel without the fear of attacks that had previously disrupted movement. “The other thing that reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. All the challenges we had travelling on that road because of fear of attack, today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he said. The sit-at-home was initially called by IPOB in 2021 in solidarity with its detained leader, Nnamdi Kanu. Although the order was later suspended in 2026, fear of attacks continued to keep businesses and public activity subdued on some Mondays. Mbah said the state deployed its “distress response squad” along the route, rather than setting up roadblocks, and asked residents of Nsukka, Enugu West and Enugu East to watch for changes around them. “We do not have roadblocks, but we have the watchful eyes of our distress response squad across the entire stretch. So, Nsukka, Ndi Enugu West, Ndi Enugu East, maybe we should even start with Nsukka: what is changing around you?” the governor said. He urged residents to see the area’s development as evidence of transformation. “Can you just look around and you can see it? This is transformation,” Mbah added. Amupitan noted that restoring public trust, enhancing operational efficiency and safeguarding the integrity of every ballot remained the central pillars of his administration. “Your arrival comes at a defining period in our national journey, as Nigeria deepens its democratic processes and advances institutional reforms ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We view your visit today as a continuation of the enduring partnership and shared commitment to democratic integrity that exists between Nigeria and the United Kingdom,” he said. Acknowledging the United Kingdom’s long-standing support through the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and development partners, Amupitan called for expanded strategic collaboration in critical areas as 2027 approaches. He listed priority partnership areas to include election cybersecurity architecture, specialised capacity building for the commission’s personnel and joint initiatives to counter artificial intelligence-driven manipulation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI). “The integrity of Nigeria’s democracy matters not only to our citizens but to the peace, stability and economic growth of the entire West African sub-region and the African continent. “We assure you and the international community that INEC remains resolutely independent, impartial and committed to delivering a 2027 general election that meets the highest global standards,” Amupitan said. Reviewing recent electoral activities, the INEC cited the successful conduct of off-cycle governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun states, alongside the FCT Area Council polls and 16 state and federal legislative by-elections. He explained that the off-cycle polls served as operational testing grounds, recording major advancements in early logistics deployment and high Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) reliability. Amupitan said that the elections also witnessed swift uploading of polling unit results on the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal as well as priority voting access for persons with disabilities (PWDs), pregnant women and the elderly. He said that with over 70 days to the 2027 general elections, the commission had successfully executed nine out of the 14 key activities outlined in its revised timetable and schedule of activities. To ensure that every registered voter exercised their franchise, Amupitan said that INEC had launched an intensive permanent voter card (PVC) collection drive, decentralised across all the 774 local government areas down to the ward registration level. item.title: Okpebholo, Oba of Benin pledge support for NDLEA drug war
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi BENIN CITY — Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, and the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, have pledged support for the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in its campaign against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking. The two leaders gave the assurance on Wednesday when the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), led the agency’s War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) advocacy campaign to Benin City. Receiving Marwa and his delegation at the Government House, Okpebholo described the fight against illicit drugs as a collective responsibility, noting that substance abuse was associated with several criminal activities. The governor, who said he had admired Marwa since his secondary school days, commended the NDLEA command in Edo State and pledged his administration’s support for its operations. “There is the need for everyone to get involved and support the fight against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking, because at the root of virtually every crime is the issue of drugs. “From our experience, even kidnappers first ask their victims for drugs before demanding ransom. That shows that illicit drug is our enemy,” he said. Okpebholo added: “Your officers and men in Edo are doing excellent work. We are ready to work with you, we are ready to partner with you, and we are ready to support you with any request you bring before us.” In his remarks, Marwa commended the governor’s support for the agency and sought his cooperation in implementing the NDLEA’s Alternative Development Programme, which encourages cannabis growers to switch to legitimate crops and sustainable livelihoods. He explained that the initiative, introduced last year, was designed to discourage illicit cannabis cultivation by providing farmers with alternatives and support for legitimate agricultural activities. According to him, the pilot phase of the programme, launched in Ondo State in January, had recorded encouraging results, prompting the agency to extend it to Edo. Marwa sought the governor’s support for the programme, as well as additional logistics assistance for NDLEA operations in the state. The highlight of the visit was the decoration of Okpebholo as a WADA Grand Ambassador in recognition of his support for the campaign against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking. Marwa and his delegation subsequently visited the Oba of Benin at his palace, where the NDLEA chairman described drug abuse as one of the major challenges confronting Nigeria. He disclosed that more than 15 million Nigerians were involved in drug abuse, representing a prevalence rate about three times the global average. Marwa said the problem had spread to schools and communities across the country, including the Benin Kingdom. item.title: Imo political rift: Onyekwere urges Tinubu to intervene
item.description: By Precious Enaike A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief Onyekachi Onyekwere, has called on President Bola Tinubu to intervene in the political disagreement between Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma and former governor Rochas Okorocha. Onyekwere, who spoke with journalists in Lagos, said resolving the differences between the two politicians was important to strengthening the APC and its mobilisation efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged the people of Imo State to support Uzodimma, whom he described as a politician with considerable influence and mobilisation capacity in the South-East. “This is the best way to deliver the President come January 2027, and his efforts and commitment have never been in doubt. I would equally call on the President to urgently intervene in this matter. “This is because the achievements of Governor Uzodimma speak volumes and, as an achiever, he is following the commendable footsteps of President Tinubu towards making Nigeria a better place to live,” he said. Onyekwere also called on the people of Abia State to support the APC governorship candidate, Eric Opia, whom he described as young and vibrant. He urged APC members in the South-East to close ranks and work towards strengthening the party’s electoral fortunes in the region. “Igbos should not allow disagreements to weaken the ruling party, APC, in their land, and all efforts should be made to achieve success. Both Governor Uzodimma and Opia have worked very hard and deserve victory at the polls,” he said. He expressed confidence that the South-East would benefit from supporting Tinubu and politicians in the region working towards his re-election. Onyekwere also praised the relationship between Tinubu and Uzodimma, saying the Federal Government’s support had contributed to development efforts in Imo State. item.title: World leaders hope for reset after US midterms
item.description: World leaders voiced hopes for a reset with the United States on Wednesday after voters delivered a huge midterm election defeat to President Donald Trump and his Republican party. The Democrats seized control of both Senate and the House of Representatives, giving them the power to block legislation and hold up Trump’s appointments. – Germany – German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he hoped to see new initiatives to end the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. “With their majority in both chambers of Congress, the Democratic Party will likely seek to shift the political course in the United States,” Wadephul said. Through cooperation between the United States and Europe, “there may be a new opportunity to launch a fresh initiative” to resolve conflicts, he said. – Spain – Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said Trump’s defeat showed that the global far-right was on the wane. “It happened in Brazil. It just happened in the US. And it will soon happen in Spain,” the socialist leader said, with elections looming later this month. The far-right wave is “no longer growing, it is unravelling,” he added. – Russia – Russia hopes Trump will continue his “peacemaking efforts” after the midterm elections, the Kremlin said. “President Trump continues to exercise his powers. We sincerely hope that he will also continue his peacemaking efforts,” spokesman Dmitry Peskov said. – South Africa – South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the result could thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington. “We’re hoping that on a bilateral basis, there will be a coming together of minds where we will find a proper path forward on geopolitics as well as on trade matters and investment matters,” he said. He added that he hoped the result would “introduce a new era in world relations”. – EU – The EU’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas voiced hope the new US Congress would support Ukraine and ramp up pressure on Russia. “I hope that the new Congress… will continue supporting Ukraine and also putting more pressure on Russia,” she said, adding that Europe and the United States “are much stronger together” in pushing Moscow to end its war. – UK – UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the result was an opportunity for the world to “unite” around resolving cost-of-living issues. “President Trump has accepted the results, and I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that’s the cost of living,” Burnham said. item.title: Ooni urges stricter enforcement of plastic recycling policies
item.description: By Ruth Eke The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to strengthen the enforcement of recycling policies to tackle the growing problem of plastic waste in Nigeria. The monarch made the call during the official opening of Polysmart Packaging Ltd., a Nigerian-owned recycling company in Ogun State. He expressed concern over the indiscriminate disposal of plastic bottles and other waste materials on roads and drainage systems, warning that the practice posed serious environmental challenges. Oba Ogunwusi, who commended the company for investing in waste recycling and environmental protection, questioned why many Nigerians found it difficult to maintain clean surroundings, unlike countries where environmental laws were strictly enforced. He noted that plastic waste was particularly difficult to manage because of its long decomposition period, adding that improper disposal would continue to undermine environmental sanitation. Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of Polysmart Packaging Ltd., Wasiu Balogun, said the company’s newly expanded $60 million facility would significantly increase plastic waste recycling capacity in Nigeria. Balogun said the company began operations in 2013 with an initial capital of N2 million but had since expanded to meet growing demand for plastic waste recycling. He said the company would collaborate with relevant regulatory agencies to promote proper plastic waste management and assist manufacturers in complying with environmental regulations. According to him, plans are underway to establish a network of waste collection agents across Nigeria’s 774 local government areas to improve the recovery and recycling of plastic materials. Balogun disclosed that the facility would process 100,000 tonnes of mixed plastics annually when it reaches full capacity. He said the capacity was equivalent to approximately 6.5 billion PET bottles, or about 15 million bottles daily. The initiative, he added, would reduce the volume of plastic bottles dumped in landfills, burnt or washed into the Atlantic Ocean. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Polysmart Packaging Ltd., Niyi Yusuf, said the facility demonstrated confidence in Nigeria’s industrial sector. Yusuf described the plant as Africa’s largest food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) facility, saying it would position Nigeria as a major recycling hub in West Africa. He said Nigeria could strengthen its recycling system through improved extended producer responsibility policies and investment in waste collection and processing infrastructure. Yusuf cited Germany, South Korea and the Netherlands as examples of countries that had developed effective recycling systems through stronger policies and infrastructure. item.title: Two allegedly shot as ADC supporters head to Atiku rally in Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Two persons believed to be supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) were allegedly shot by operatives of the Sokoto State Community Guards along the Sokoto–Wurno Road on Wednesday, amid heightened political tension ahead of the party’s presidential campaign rally in the state. The incident reportedly occurred when the operatives barricaded the road linking Sokoto metropolis with the eastern part of the state, forcing vehicles conveying supporters to the rally venue to turn back. The victims were said to be among those travelling to attend the campaign rally for the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in Sokoto. Eyewitnesses alleged that the shooting followed an altercation between occupants of a vehicle conveying the supporters and the Community Guards. The operatives were accused of opening fire during the confrontation, leaving two persons with gunshot injuries. The victims were subsequently rushed to a hospital for medical attention. The development has raised concerns over the safety of political supporters and freedom of movement during campaign activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. A source said it took the intervention of the Civilian JTF in the convoy of Senator Ibrahim Lamido, coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, before vehicles were allowed to move through the checkpoint. The latest incident comes amid existing tensions between the ADC and security operatives in the state. The Community Guards had previously been accused of attacking the ADC governorship candidate, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto. The latest allegation has further heightened concerns over the conduct of security personnel and the need to ensure that political activities take place without intimidation or violence. However, when contacted, the Sokoto State Police Command Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufai, said the command had yet to receive information about the alleged shooting. He said he could not confirm the incident. The post Two allegedly shot as ADC supporters head to Atiku rally in Sokoto appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Igbo youths give INEC chairman seven-day ultimatum over commissioner
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Pan-Igbo Youth Assembly (PIYA) has given the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, seven days to redeploy National Commissioner Ken Nnamdi Ukeagu from supervising Imo, Anambra and Ebonyi states. The group threatened to occupy INEC offices across the South-East and the commission’s national headquarters in Abuja if its demand was not met within the stipulated period. PIYA also announced plans to mobilise Igbo youths for demonstrations across the five South-East states, other parts of the country and the diaspora should INEC fail to act. The group said the seven-day ultimatum was sufficient for the commission to take an administrative decision capable of restoring public confidence in its operations. It, however, assured that the planned protests would be lawful and orderly, insisting that its campaign was aimed at demanding institutional accountability and electoral neutrality. The group also called on the Presidency, National Assembly, Council of State, civil society organisations, traditional rulers and religious leaders to prevail on INEC to address the controversy. PIYA made the demands in a statement issued by its spokesman, Comrade Noble Nkem Regius, in which it accused Ukeagu of alleged partisan conduct and political engagements with opposition figures. It claimed that the allegations had created a crisis of confidence in the electoral umpire, particularly as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. item.title: Senate halts processing of bills for new universities
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has directed its committees to suspend the processing of bills seeking the establishment of new universities and other tertiary institutions in line with the Federal Government’s policy. The directive, which particularly affects the Committees on Tertiary Institutions and Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), is aimed at ensuring that existing institutions are adequately developed and strengthened before new ones are established. Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), announced the directive on Wednesday, urging lawmakers to respect the government’s position on the matter. Bamidele said the policy was necessary to allow existing universities and other tertiary institutions to consolidate their operations and improve infrastructure before additional institutions were considered. He urged the Clerk of the Senate, Dr Emmanuel Odo, to guide lawmakers on the policy, noting that some legislators might not be aware of the Federal Government’s position. The Senate Leader also advised education committees to avoid presenting bills seeking the establishment of new institutions for consideration during plenary. He acknowledged that lawmakers sometimes found it difficult to turn down requests from colleagues seeking legislative support for the establishment of universities and other tertiary institutions. Supporting the directive, Senate President Godswill Akpabio disclosed that President Bola Tinubu had discussed the matter with the leadership of the National Assembly. Akpabio said the President was opposed to establishing new universities, polytechnics and other tertiary institutions for the next five to seven years. He explained that the proposed moratorium was intended to give existing institutions time to develop their infrastructure and commence effective academic operations. The Senate President observed that several recently established universities existed largely on paper, with some yet to secure permanent sites or complete the necessary site-clearance processes. He stressed that establishing a university was a serious national responsibility that should not be treated with the same simplicity as setting up primary schools. According to him, universities are national institutions expected to admit students from different parts of the country, irrespective of their geographical locations. Akpabio added that the Federal Government had made efforts to ensure an equitable distribution of universities across the country, making it necessary to consolidate existing investments rather than continue establishing new institutions. He consequently directed the Clerk of the Senate to ensure that bills seeking the establishment of new tertiary institutions were no longer listed for consideration. The Senate subsequently adjourned plenary until Tuesday next week. The post Senate halts processing of bills for new universities appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout
item.description: Iran’s supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress. The results could constrain Trump’s ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes. “Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement Wednesday. He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages. Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms. “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X. “If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said. Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war. Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party. “I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I’ve done,” Trump told Fox News. On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession. “They built an anti-aircraft facility… As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely,” Trump told US media, but he called it a “minor attack”. – ‘Locked and loaded’ – Earlier this week the president said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. item.title: Step-by-step: How to download NIN slip online for free
item.description: The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has explained how Nigerians can download their National Identification Number (NIN) slips online for free through its NINAuth mobile application. The commission said the service allows registered NIN holders to obtain their official identification slips directly on their mobile phones without visiting NIMC enrolment centres or paying third-party agents. NIMC demonstrated the process in a video shared on its official X account on Wednesday, outlining the steps users must follow to access and download the document. According to the commission, Nigerians can obtain their NIN slips by completing a few steps on the NINAuth application. How to download your NIN slip using the NINAuth app NIN holders who wish to download their identification slips are required to follow these steps: Download the NINAuth application from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Open the application on your mobile phone. Tap the “Do More with NINAuth” option. Select “NIN Slip” from the available services. Complete the facial authentication process to verify your identity. Once authentication is successful, select “Download NIN Slip” to generate the document. Save the downloaded slip on your mobile phone for future use. NIMC explained that successful facial verification would allow users to access and download their official identification slips directly through the application. “Once verified, click on ‘Download NIN Slip’ to generate and save the official NIMC-issued NIN slip into your mobile phone,” the commission said. It described the service as a convenient and secure way for Nigerians to access their identification documents, stressing that the process was free. “It is that simple, it is free, available, and a few taps away. Get yours today,” NIMC added. What is a National Identification Number (NIN)? The National Identification Number is an 11-digit unique identification number issued by NIMC to Nigerians and legal residents following successful registration. It serves as a means of establishing and verifying an individual’s identity and links their personal records to the National Identity Database. The number is used for identity verification across several sectors, including banking, telecommunications, government services and other official transactions. item.title: ‘Show your certificates’ — Amaechi replies Oshiomhole over ‘shallow’ comment
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, has challenged Senator Adams Oshiomhole to present his academic certificates after the former Edo State governor described him as “shallow”. Amaechi issued the challenge during an interview on Rapid TV while responding to Oshiomhole’s recent criticism of his political positions and credibility. Oshiomhole had described Amaechi as “shallow” and “unreliable”, accusing him of contradicting his previous positions by criticising the All Progressives Congress (APC) and President Bola Tinubu after previously supporting the party. The former APC national chairman also questioned Amaechi’s relationship with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, recalling that Amaechi had previously challenged Atiku’s emergence as the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential candidate. Reacting, Amaechi said he was disappointed by Oshiomhole’s remarks, insisting that the two men were political equals who served as governors at the same time. “He said I’m shallow, but I hold degrees in Law and Literature, Master’s degrees in both fields, and a certificate from the University of London. I also have a master’s degree from King’s College London, and I’m pursuing a master’s degree in Global Political Economy,” Amaechi said. “Tell him to show his certificate,” he said. The former governor also cited his academic qualifications, including a certificate from the University of London and a master’s degree from King’s College London, challenging Oshiomhole to make his own educational credentials public. Amaechi further recalled that Oshiomhole was among the governors who elected him chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, questioning why the senator would now describe him as shallow. He said, “He’s not my subordinate. We are equals. He was governor while I was governor. So he’s not my subordinate.” Amaechi also linked Oshiomhole’s criticism to his role in the removal of the former Edo governor as chairman of the APC, alleging that he led the team that worked against his continued leadership of the party. “What is paining Oshiomhole is that he was removed as chairman of the party, and I led the team that removed him as chairman of the party because he was incapable of governing the party,” he said. Oshiomhole had also questioned Amaechi’s credibility by recalling his previous criticism of Atiku, claiming the former Rivers governor once described the primary that produced Atiku as the PDP presidential candidate as fraudulent and challenged his emergence in court. He further alleged that Amaechi changed his position after Atiku approached him to work together. item.title: Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, for Abuja after completing his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the holy city of Makkah. According to a statement by the presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s aircraft took off from the Royal Terminal of the airport at exactly 5:13 p.m. Saudi time. Onanuga said the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Consul-General, Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the President to the airport. Before his departure, Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. ﻿ The President had earlier led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers. Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the President offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people. He also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would become a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity. Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport before departing Saudi Arabia. Onanuga said the President’s visit to Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as a renewed commitment to building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation. The statement added that Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers. “President Tinubu left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all,” the statement said. Those in the President’s entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. item.title: Army chief lists 28,000 recruitment, 12 divisions as achievements
item.description: ….Shaibu highlights 681 housing units, operational expansion in first year By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has highlighted the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel and the provision of 681 housing units as some of his major achievements in his first year in office. Shaibu disclosed this in a goodwill message to officers, soldiers, civilian staff and their families, published on the Nigerian Army’s X handle on Wednesday to mark his first 365 days as Chief of Army Staff. He said the Federal Government’s approval for the expansion of the Army and recruitment of additional personnel represented significant steps towards strengthening its capacity to address the country’s security challenges. “One of the most significant achievements in the past year is the Federal Government’s approval to expand the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, along with the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel,” he said. According to him, the expansion is aimed at strengthening territorial coverage, improving operational responsiveness, enhancing the protection of vulnerable communities and providing greater capacity for sustained security operations across the country. The Army chief said his administration had focused on improving operational effectiveness, institutional capacity and professional standards in line with the constitutional responsibilities of the service. He explained that the Army’s transformation agenda was guided by five strategic pillars: Professional Excellence, Robust Administration, Operational Readiness, Strategic Cooperation and Exemplary Leadership. He said the pillars were anchored on a Soldier-First Culture, which prioritises the welfare, motivation, dignity and professional development of personnel. Shaibu commended officers and soldiers serving in various operational theatres, particularly those engaged in operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to national security. “I particularly commend our gallant officers and soldiers serving in the various operational theatres, especially those engaged in ongoing operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to our national security,” he said. He also paid tribute to personnel who had died in the line of duty, acknowledging their sacrifices in the service of the country. “I acknowledge with profound respect the sacrifices of personnel who have paid the supreme price in the service of our fatherland and honour their memory,” he said. The COAS also extended his appreciation to wounded personnel undergoing recovery and urged all officers and soldiers to maintain professionalism, respect human rights and comply with the rules of engagement while carrying out their duties. item.title: Ogun monarch drags Abiodun to court over suspension
item.description: Seeks reinstatement, injunction against enforcement of suspension order By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Ebenezer Akintunde Akinyemi, has dragged Governor Dapo Abiodun and four other respondents before the Federal High Court in Abeokuta over his suspension by the state government. The monarch is seeking an interim injunction restraining the governor and other respondents from enforcing the suspension order issued on October 20, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the substantive suit. In the suit marked FHC/AB/FHR/148/26, Oba Akinyemi alleged that the state government suspended him without prior notice or giving him an opportunity to respond to the allegations against him. Other respondents are the Ogun State Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Nigeria Police Force and the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State. In an ex parte motion dated October 23, 2026, filed before the Abeokuta Judicial Division of the Federal High Court, the monarch asked the court to restrain the respondents, their agents and officers from implementing or giving effect to the suspension letter. He also sought an order restraining the respondents from compelling him to vacate the Eselu Palace, preventing him from presenting himself as the traditional ruler or stopping him from wearing his crown and other royal insignia. Additionally, he asked the court to restrain the respondents from harassing, intimidating, arresting or detaining him, or otherwise interfering with his exercise of the rights and functions of his office. The monarch also wants the court to direct the Commissioner of Police and officers under his command not to take any steps to enforce the suspension pending the determination of the application and the substantive suit. In a 12-paragraph affidavit supporting the application, Oba Akinyemi stated that he received a letter dated October 20, 2026, from the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, notifying him of his immediate suspension as the Eselu of Iselu Kingdom. According to him, the letter directed him to vacate the palace immediately, stop presenting himself as the traditional ruler and refrain from wearing or using any royal paraphernalia. He, however, challenged the procedure adopted by the state government, alleging that he was neither given prior notice of the intended suspension nor afforded an opportunity to defend himself against the allegations. In paragraph six of the affidavit, he stated: “That I was never given any prior notice or opportunity to be heard before the suspension was imposed on the allegation alleged.” He argued that the government’s action raised constitutional issues bordering on his right to fair hearing as guaranteed under the 1999 Constitution, as amended. item.title: Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement
item.description: Lawmakers divided over proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to regulate rental payments and curb exploitative practices by landlords and estate agents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), amid disagreements among lawmakers over a proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments. The bill, sponsored by Rep. Paul Sunday Nnamchi, seeks to regulate advance rent payments, arbitrary rent increases and agency fees, as well as establish a unified digital register for housing agents. It also provides safeguards for landlords and tenants, with penalties for violations of its provisions. Leading the debate, Nnamchi said the rising cost of accommodation and excessive demands for advance rent had placed enormous financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, small businesses and employment mobility. He said the proposed legislation was designed to establish a fairer and more accountable rental system through the regulation of advance payments, reasonable limits on agency fees and proper identification of housing agents. “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns. “Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation,” he said. Supporting the bill, Rep. Idris Zacharias, representing Ida/Igalamela/Ibaji/Ofu Federal Constituency of Kogi State, described the proposal as important but called for broader consideration of land administration and housing challenges in the FCT. He also urged the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to be included in the committee that would consider the bill. Similarly, Rep. Chinedu Ogah, representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency of Ebonyi State, backed the proposal, citing the difficulties businesses face in securing office accommodation in Abuja. Ogah said renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between N25 million and N30 million annually, excluding additional agency charges. He argued that regulating the rental market would provide clearer rules for transactions and encourage investment in the sector. However, Rep. Leko Jafaru Gambo, representing Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for a review of the bill’s title, arguing that the word “prohibit” should be replaced with “regulate”. He also suggested that the legislation should have nationwide application, but Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu clarified that its current scope was limited to the FCT. Rep. Ibe Okwara Osonwa, representing Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, also supported regulation but cautioned against an outright prohibition of multi-year rent arrangements. item.title: Lagos Opens Legal Research Centre, Targets Stronger Justice Delivery
item.description: The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal expertise and prepare the state’s justice institutions for emerging challenges. Established by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, the Centre is expected to serve as a hub for legal research, professional training, policy development and capacity building for practitioners and public officials in the justice sector. Speaking at the official opening ceremony in Alausa, Ikeja, on Wednesday, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN, described the facility as more than another government building, saying it represents a deliberate investment in knowledge, institutional excellence and the future of justice administration in Lagos State. “There are occasions when we open a building or office. There are other occasions when we open a door to the future. Today, in Lagos, we are doing the latter — opening a door to the future,” Pedro said. He described the Centre as the first of its kind within a Ministry of Justice in Nigeria, arguing that a justice system that intends to remain relevant and effective must continually educate, examine and reform itself. Dignitaries at the opening of the Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training in Lagos. Pedro said the initiative aligns with the broader development agenda of the Sanwo-Olu administration, noting that the development of Lagos cannot be separated from strong institutions and an efficient administration of justice. He identified the rule of law, access to justice and capable institutions as essential foundations for economic development, good governance and social inclusion. The Attorney-General also linked the Centre to the administration’s THEMES Plus Agenda, stressing that building a secure, economically vibrant and inclusive society requires sustained investment in the people and institutions responsible for interpreting, administering and developing the state’s laws. He said the Centre would help address the growing demands of a modern justice system, including the need for continuous professional development, evidence-based policy and institutional reform. Outlining its proposed operational framework, Pedro disclosed that the Ministry intends to incorporate the Centre as a not-for-profit entity under a public-private partnership arrangement. Under the proposed structure, the Ministry of Justice and its private-sector partners will jointly manage the Centre’s day-to-day operations. While the government will provide policy direction, legitimacy and strategic oversight, the private sector is expected to contribute funding, technical expertise, innovation and operational efficiency. Pedro said the arrangement was designed to ensure the Centre’s sustainability and effectiveness. The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN. item.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
item.description: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments. The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. “This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. “I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l) But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration. Republican Heartland Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008. In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule. Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers. In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024. item.title: How military reduced nationwide attacks by 73 per cent in October as 217 terrorists neutralised
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian military have drastically reduced attacks across various theatres of operations in October 2026, Daily Trust reports. Checks showed that only 98 attacks were recorded during the month under review, representing a 73.3 per cent decline from the 367 attacks recorded in September. A breakdown of the October figures showed that Operation Enduring Peace recorded the highest number of attacks with 29 incidents, followed by Operation Hadin Kai with 27 and Operation Fansan Yamma with 24. Operation Whirl Stroke recorded 12 attacks, while Operation Udo Ka recorded four. Operations Delta Safe and Savannah Shield recorded one attack each. Specifically, the October figure represents a decline of 269 attacks compared with the previous month’s total of 367. This is just as the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, assured Nigerians that the military would intensify efforts to apprehend those responsible for the attacks and bring them to justice. Oluyede also urged troops to remain disciplined, uphold the rules of engagement and respect human rights, while warning against complacency, particularly as the festive season approaches. He called on security agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and joint planning, while urging community leaders and residents to report suspicious activities to security formations or through the military’s toll-free line, 193. Providing updates for Nigerians on military operations across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that many kidnapped victims would continue to be freed from captivity. “During the period under review, the AFN recorded a total of 98 attacks across various theatres of operation. Operation HADIN KAI recorded 27 attacks, Operation FANSAN YAMMA recorded 24, Operation ENDURING PEACE recorded 29, Operation WHIRL STROKE recorded 12, Operation UDO KA (OPUK) recorded 4, while Operation DELTA SAFE and Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD recorded 1 attack each,” the breakdown was contained in a document released on Friday. Earlier in September, Operation Enduring Peace recorded 147 attacks, Operation Fansan Yamma 115, Operation Whirl Stroke 55, Operation Hadin Kai 33, Operation Savannah Shield 13 and Operation Udo Ka four, while Operation Delta Safe recorded none. The senior military officer explained that troops neutralised more than 217 terrorists and criminals, arrested 333 suspects and rescued 349 kidnap victims during the month. He added that 70 insurgents surrendered to troops, while 105 arms and 3,174 rounds of ammunition were recovered.
